items.title: Norris wins wet São Paulo race as Mercedes clinches Constructors’ title
items.summary: Formula1.com reports Norris won the 71-lap wet-dry-wet race in 1:35:23.504, 14.602 seconds ahead of Verstappen; Hadjar completed the podium. Mercedes clinched the 2026 Constructors’ title. Verstappen also received the official fan-voted Driver of the Day award with 31.3% of votes. The published 22-entrant Race classification is still marked provisional.
items.why_it_matters: Norris converted pole while Verstappen climbed from P21 and won the fan vote; Mercedes' Constructors’ title is decided, but the live classification remains subject to revision.

items.title: Antonelli, Leclerc and Bearman penalised as Race classification remains provisional
items.summary: FIA Document 80 gives Kimi Antonelli five seconds added to Race time for Car 12's unsafe release into Franco Colapinto's path, resolving Documents 68-69. Document 79 gives Charles Leclerc five seconds for contact with Liam Lawson at Turn 12, resolving Documents 72-73; the Stewards found the contact helped Leclerc pass five corners later and cited wet conditions and minor contact in reducing the penalty from ten seconds. Document 78 gives Oliver Bearman five seconds for an unsafe release into Leclerc's path, resolving Documents 74-75. Document 76 lists 22 Race lap-time deletions across ten drivers; Document 77 reports all inspected items and weights complied. Formula1.com's 21:36 UTC Race table still contains 22 entrants and marks the classification provisional.
items.why_it_matters: Three five-second penalties, separate lap-time deletions and a routine scrutineering report must not be conflated; the latest published classification remains provisional.

items.title: Hamilton reaches 400 starts and scores in São Paulo
items.summary: Formula1.com identifies the São Paulo Grand Prix as Hamilton’s 400th F1 start; the provisional classification places him ninth, one lap down, with two points.
items.why_it_matters: A career milestone sits alongside a points finish after starting 20th; both remain tied to the current provisional classification.

items.title: Verstappen describes his P21-to-podium drive as a challenging race
items.summary: Formula1.com reports Verstappen started P21, reached second after a strong opening intermediate stint and finished 14.602 seconds behind Norris. He said the car later had a "weird balance"; Hadjar completed a Red Bull double podium in third.
items.why_it_matters: The comeback and changing conditions shaped the podium battle, but Verstappen's account of the balance issue is his description, not a confirmed technical diagnosis.
